pending.body: The legacy nitrogen kinetics param_meta migration in `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs` (around line 2172-2205) moves metadata verbatim from legacy keys (e.g. `aob_k_tan_mg`) to canonical keys (e.g. `aob_k_tan_mg_n_per_l`) via `move_legacy_process_param_meta_key()`, but the associated `valid_range` and `unit` fields are not transformed to match the new scale. When `legacy_total_param_to_mg_per_l()` converts a whole-tank-total value to a concentration, the metadata's `valid_range` may no longer be semantically correct for the transformed value. Either the migration should also transform `valid_range` bounds by the same scaling factor, or range-checking of migrated legacy parameters should be skipped/warned.

Nitrifier kinetic rate parameters `decomposer_vmax_per_hour`, `decomposer_growth_yield`, `decomposer_decay_rate_per_hour`, and all AOB/NOB/comammox `vmax`, `growth_yield`, and `decay_rate` fields in `process/default.toml` lack `param_meta` entries despite being equally load-bearing for cycling speed as the K_s half-saturation constants that ARE annotated. The acceptance criteria require provenance for 'AOB/NOB/comammox K_s values (nitrogen kinetics)' but the K_s values alone are insufficient — without knowing the confidence of vmax and yield, a calibration bead cannot prioritize which rate constants to tune. Add at minimum a heuristic or placeholder `param_meta` block for each vmax and growth_yield parameter.

The `ATMOSPHERIC_CO2_PPM` constant in `crates/tank_core/src/systems/chemistry.rs:17` is hardcoded to 410.0 with no provenance comment. This value directly affects Henry's law CO2 equilibrium calculations and all downstream carbonate chemistry. It should have at minimum a one-line comment noting the source (e.g., NOAA global average ~2020) and that it is treated as a fixed constant for the current model scope.

Significant maintainability risk: the new alkalinity accounting stores meq values in APIs and fields that are explicitly named as mg, including `ElementBudget.in_mg/out_mg/net_mg` in `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7/crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:35-56`, the alkalinity field docs in `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7/crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:72-76`, the concrete assignment in `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7/crates/tank_core/src/systems/water_change.rs:149-152`, and the helper/assertion surface in `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7/crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:64-83` plus `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7/crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:418-507`. This removes unit safety from the type system and makes it easy for later callers to mix mg and meq tolerances or diagnostics without the compiler catching it.
